#2768. Ja’Marr Chase has spectacular showing in Bengals’ big win vs. Steelers

Ja'Marr Chase said he loves primetime games. On Sunday night, he showed everyone why.

Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals' 38-18 win over Pittsburgh at Paycor. It was the fourth 200-yard game of his career and the third-best yardage total he's ever had, and it came against a Steelers team that walked in tied for first in the AFC North and walked out a game behind.

Chase didn't find the end zone, and it didn't matter. He was the engine of the drives that buried Pittsburgh early. His two deep shots, a 53-yarder and a 43-yarder, each set up Bengals touchdowns. The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions and took a 24-3 lead into the locker room, while the Steelers managed just 40 total yards and four first downs before halftime.

The only thing that stopped Chase was the scoreboard. With the game in hand, the Bengals eased off in the fourth quarter and brought in Joe Flacco for mop-up duty.

Sunday was Chase's fourth regular-season game with at least 200 receiving yards.

The headline record of the night belonged to his quarterback. Burrow threw four touchdown passes, giving him five straight games with at least four total touchdowns, which ties Peyton Manning's 2004 run for the longest such streak in NFL history. The Bengals also completed 21 passes before Aaron Rodgers completed his first, tying the most by one team before its opponent's first completion since 1978.

None of that happens without No. 1 stretching the defense. When Chase is getting behind safeties like he did Sunday night, everything underneath opens up for Chase Brown, Drew Sample, and Dohnte Meyers, which is exactly how all four touchdown passes were scored.

The Bengals are 7-2 and alone in first place in the AFC North. And their best player just reminded everyone that the bigger the stage, the better he gets.

#2762. Christian McCaffrey on career-high receiving yards: You just catch it and run as fast as you can

The 49ers running back had never had more than 121 receiving yards in a single game. He had 161 receiving yards on four catches Sunday against the Cowboys, scoring on catch-and-runs of 74 and 66 in the 49ers’ 46-40 win.

“You never know,” McCaffrey said. “You go into each game. You don’t really predict anything. Again, you just have to have the right mindset on a play that’s going to break. You trust your instincts and play fast.”

His first receiving touchdown came when Brock Purdy rolled to his right to buy time and found McCaffrey running free on the scramble drill.

“It really is backyard football at that point,” McCaffrey said. “We all played it as kids at recess, and you draw up plays on your hand, and it never happens. You ever tell a 5-year-old to run a post route, and he just runs a corner and something else, but he’s open? That’s kind of what that was. Again, I think those little decisions that you make in games, from Brock to scramble, not to just surrender the play but to keep it alive. That’s a big deal. There’s no planning that goes into that. It’s just him doing a great job playing ball.”

What turned out to be the game-winning touchdown came with 3:23 remaining when Purdy found McCaffrey, who was matched up against Von Miller, over the middle.

“They brought pressure,” McCaffrey said. “They dropped a D-end on me, so that’s a perfect look for that play. Again, it was a great job by Brock getting the ball where it needed to be. It made it easy for me.

“You just catch it and run as fast as you can to try to score. Don’t overthink it. You hope that nobody catches you, and you hope that you’re really fast so your teammates don’t catch up to you to celebrate, because it makes you look slow. We’ll have to check the tape.”

McCaffrey had a 16-yard touchdown run and 62 yards rushing. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown.

#2760. Four things to watch as Sixers look to respond against Raptors

Four things to watch as Sixers look to respond against Raptors originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers will not need to wait long for an opportunity to move past their most lopsided loss of the season.

Less than 48 hours after Boston's 123-101 win exposed several of Philadelphia's early weaknesses, the Sixers will host the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

The Raptors are coming off a difficult meeting with the Celtics, too. Toronto led Boston by 22 points Wednesday before being outscored 61-34 over the final 29:24 of a 98-93 loss.

Philadelphia enters at 9-3 following Tuesday's defeat. Toronto is 5-6 and will complete a back-to-back and its third game in four nights.

LeBron James has been ruled out because of low-back and sciatica management. Joel Embiid is questionable with right plantar fascia injury management. Toronto will be without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Nate Bittle.

Here are four areas to watch as the Sixers try to respond.

Few teams have forced opponents into mistakes as frequently as Toronto.

The Raptors have generated 18.9 turnovers per game, the highest mark in the NBA. They are also averaging 10.9 steals and nearly 15 offensive rebounds.

The Sixers have countered that type of pressure well. Their 13.0 turnovers per game are tied for one of the lowest marks in the league.

Toronto's length remains disruptive even without Leonard and Barnes. The Raptors regularly crowd ball handlers, reach into passing lanes and send multiple players toward the offensive glass. Jakob Poeltl supplies size inside while RJ Barrett, Ja'Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles can create problems away from the ball.

The Raptors' pressure can punish a careless pass twice. It takes away a Sixers possession and gives Toronto an opportunity to score before the defense gets organized.

Philadelphia has largely avoided those mistakes while adjusting to a new lineup and playing at a quicker pace. Maintaining that control without James, who has handled a significant share of the playmaking, will be one of Thursday's clearest challenges.

Toronto has not built its offense around half-court shooting.

The Raptors are averaging 49.6 paint points and 16.4 fast-break points. Even while shorthanded Wednesday, they scored 18 points in transition against Boston.

That presents a direct test for a Sixers defense allowing 16.5 fast-break points per game, the fourth-highest figure in the NBA. Philadelphia has also surrendered 49.5 paint points per contest.

The first concern will be slowing the ball.

Immanuel Quickley returned Wednesday after missing two games with right hamstring soreness. He gives Toronto another guard capable of attacking early in the shot clock, while Barrett has consistently looked to get downhill with Leonard and Barnes unavailable.

Poeltl can create scoring chances without having a play called for him. He runs the floor, screens for Toronto's guards, rolls toward the rim and cleans up misses.

The Sixers have been effective in transition themselves, averaging 17.1 fast-break points. Maxey and VJ Edgecombe can change ends quickly after a stop, but Philadelphia must secure the ball first.

Thursday's game could swing on which team gets to run and which one is forced to create against a set defense.

Toronto provided an extreme example Wednesday of how quickly the three-point line can alter a game.

The Raptors entered their matchup against Boston shooting 31.8 percent from beyond the arc. They proceeded to hit 10 of their 18 attempts in the first quarter, tying a franchise record for threes in a period.

They went 6 for 25 over the final three quarters.

After Wednesday, Toronto is shooting 32.4 percent from three this season. The Sixers should not treat the Raptors like an elite perimeter team. They also cannot allow them to find early confidence through uncovered catch-and-shoot attempts.

Walter made five threes Wednesday and scored a team-high 17 points. Rookie Allen Graves added 13 points, while Quickley, Barrett and Jamison Battle are all willing shooters when the ball reaches them in rhythm.

Philadelphia's problems against Boston extended beyond the Celtics making difficult shots. The Sixers were late on several closeouts and occasionally allowed too much separation while navigating screens.

Toronto does not rely on the three as heavily as Boston. Wednesday showed it can still build a lead quickly when those shots start falling.

The Raptors expended significant energy Wednesday before traveling to Philadelphia.

They scored 38 first-quarter points, built a 22-point lead and then watched Boston erase the entire margin before the end of the third quarter. Quickley and Barrett each played more than 31 minutes. Poeltl and Walter both played at least 29.

The Sixers should have the fresher legs. Whether they take advantage could become apparent early.

Philadelphia has averaged 26.3 first-quarter points with a minus-2.2 scoring margin in opening periods. Slow starts have forced the Sixers to play from behind several times, including in their 29-point comeback against Cleveland.

An aggressive start would make Toronto respond quickly after a draining loss. Maxey and Edgecombe can apply pressure by pushing the ball after defensive rebounds instead of allowing the Raptors to set their pressure defense.

James' absence will require an adjustment. Maxey, Brown and Anfernee Simons should handle more of the ball and more of the decisions that come with initiating the offense.

If Embiid plays, the Sixers can make Toronto work through Poeltl by establishing him inside. If Embiid sits, Philadelphia's size concerns will become more pronounced with Adem Bona, Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti also unavailable.

The Sixers have a rest advantage against a depleted opponent coming off an emotional loss. Their response should begin well before the fourth quarter.

#2758. Christian McCaffrey, 49ers run past Cowboys 46-40

49ers fans took over AT&T Stadium on Sunday, out-drawing and out-yelling Cowboys fans. They booed the Cowboys running onto their own field, and they loudly celebrated a 46-40 San Francisco win.

In an entertaining game, the 49ers moved to 8-1, and the Cowboys fell to 4-6.

Christian McCaffrey had a career-high 161 receiving yards on four catches, two of them touchdowns, and ran for 62 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown.

The 49ers led 38-19 with 11:26 remaining in the fourth quarter. But George Pickens caught a 5-yard touchdown pass, which was followed by a missed 2-point conversion. Ryan Flournoy’s 11-yard score with 3:42 left cut the Cowboys’ deficit to 38-32. The 49ers burned only 2:26 on their possession in between, punting after four plays.

The 49ers showed the Cowboys who they are, though, when Brock Purdy hit McCaffrey across the middle of the field. Von Miller, who was covering McCaffrey, and his teammates had no chance of catching the running back, who went 66 yards to the end zone.

The Cowboys didn’t go away quietly, scoring once more on CeeDee Lamb’s 1-yard reception. Dak Prescott ran in the 2-point conversion.

Dallas tried an onside kick despite having three timeouts and did not convert.

Kaelon Black, who had 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled on the second-down play. Quinnen Williams forced it, but Black was able to get back on the ball. The 49ers punted, and the Cowboys were left with only 9 seconds and in need of 91 yards and a miracle.

McCaffrey’s other touchdowns were a 74-yard reception and a 16-yard run.

The 49ers had 584 yards, the third-most the Cowboys have allowed in their history. It was not far from the 49ers’ team record of 621.

Purdy set a career-high with 389 passing yards and threw three touchdowns, completing 22 of 28 passes.

George Kittle had six catches for 74 yards, and new addition Keenan Allen five for 61. Deebo Samuel had three catches for 31 yards and a touchdown and three carries for 78 yards and a touchdown.

The Cowboys couldn’t keep up, even with 439 yards.

Prescott was 30-of-51 for 343 yards with five touchdowns and an interception. Pickens had 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns, and Lamb seven for 72 yards and a touchdown. Flournoy added six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown.

Cincinnati went head-to-head with their heated rivals, who were tied with them for the division lead. And they absolutely destroyed them.

Here are three things we learned from the clinic Burrow and the Bengals put on against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Amarius Mims dominated T.J. Watt, making him look like a child.

And Orlando Brown Jr., considered to be the weak link at the start of the season, just delivered the best pass protection game of any left tackle this year, not allowing a pressure on 44 dropbacks.

Burrow had clean pockets almost the entire game, similar to the game against the Atlanta Falcons. And, as a result, he methodically picked those defenses apart.

In the past, the Bengals would fall behind early, trying to force a run game that wasn't there.

Against the Steelers, they used the short game to get the pass in a flow, and sprinkled in deep shots down the field.

Burrow and the offense came out firing, confident in their ability to have their way with any defense, even one as intimidating as Pittsburgh's.

He's probably been the best receiver in the league for a couple of seasons, but he's somehow reached another level.

After a slow start, Chase has 527 yards receiving in his last three games. He had probably the most casual 200 yard receiving game you'll ever see against the Steelers. And his 231 total was the highest for any receiver this season.

The combination of Burrow having time, the offense finding its identity, and Tee Higgins emerging as the most physically dominant receiver in the league have led to Chase being able to break out his entire bag on a regular basis.

#2748. Cain Velasquez named GM of MMA for Combat U at Sacramento State, teases potential return to competition

Cain Velasquez will be using his knowledge in the fight game to prepare the next generation of MMA fighters.

Velasquez has been named the new GM of MMA for Combat U — a first-of-the-nation collegiate club sport for students seeking a world-class education as well as high-level opportunities for combat sports training and competition. The former UFC heavyweight champion exclusively announced his new role to MMA Fighting.

"Yeah, Sacramento State has been, for a couple of years working on a combat, program, so mixed martial arts, boxing, Muay Thai, jiu-jitsu, and wrestling as well, where they give scholarships to their athletes and they actually have them perform, " Velasquez told MMA Fighting. "So MMA athletes will fight in the cage. So I've been called upon [by] Sacramento State to be their first general manager for the mixed martial arts aspect of what they're doing, in their progress to help this sport grow and, help the sport grow at the level that these these young women, these young men, need to start at. Get them off on the right foot."

Velasquez joins a team that includes former WEC champ and multi-time UFC title challenger Urijah Faber, boxing great Andre Ward, and fellow UFC veterans Cory McKenna and Joseph Morales.

While it's one thing to prepare aspiring combat athletes to compete in their respective disciplines, it's another to be able to have everything under one roof — including things a lot of new combat athletes wouldn't think of.

"The most important thing as well is to help them get an education as well," Velasquez said. "Not just in the combat sports era, but also go into education, help them get their degrees. So I think that's very powerful. When I was fighting, it was pretty much, 'OK, you're going in to fight and then that's it.'

"But to be able to also get an education, have a school behind you, have all the programs there, have the rehab, the doctors, the nurses and everything else you need, to have that all under one roof is very important."

Velasquez is ready to take on this new challenge in a more front office role, and feels like he's jumping in at the right time.

"It's crazy to think how far and how much this sport has grown and what it's doing," Velasquez said. "Just the young kids and how much they love the sport and how it's growing everything else, it's growing jiu-jitsu, it's growing wrestling, boxing, so combat sports, in general, have just grown immensely from all the MMA promotions out there, right?

"These kids want to grow up and be a world champion in the sport, and they're doing all these different sports, and it's just elevating everything. So it's crazy to think that we're living in this day and age that a college like like Sac State is doing something like this in a big way."

As far as competition goes, it seems as if Velasquez has turned the page from MMA. But with Real American Freestyle having a rapid rise, and Velasquez having fantastic wrestling credentials from his high school and college years, the 44-year-old admits he not only has interest in competing for RAF, he's just waiting for the phone to ring.

"I think it's a possibility," Velasquez explained. "They gotta go ahead and pull the trigger, on their end. But yeah, I love the sport of wrestling. It's what's got me here. There'll always be a soft spot for me in in in wrestling, I think some of the best athletes, some of the best mixed martial artists come from it, So it's a possibility, yeah."

#2745. Oregon Ducks Football: Duck Tape Film Review Michigan Wolverines 2026

Author's note: A full transcript of the video will be available by Monday evening.

Here is a written account of my conclusions about the game for those who prefer to use the video only for play breakdowns.

Oregon won because their receivers were a mismatch against Michigan's pass coverage and Michigan's own offense is still a dysfunctional mess… but the Ducks missed a chance to put the game away early.

The score was only relatively close late into the game to due to a combination Oregon's issues at offensive line and poor play calling given the relative strengths and weaknesses of the Ducks against Michigan's defense.

The Wolverines' offense couldn't move the ball on their own merits, they could only take advantage of Oregon mistakes and the Ducks' defense didn't make enough for them to keep the game competitive.

The following players listed as "out" on the game day availability report are presumed lost for the season: QB #5 Dante Moore, DB #21 Aaron Flowers, ILB #23 Brayden Platt, OL #56 Trent Ferguson, and now OLB #44 Tatum Tuioti. Additionally DL #55 Matthew Johnson, OL #74 Dave Iuli, and RB #0 Jordan Davison have been unavailable for multiple games. Backup TE #19 Andrew Olesh was listed as Doubtful earlier this week and was Out on the game day report.

After some off the field issues, we did see WR #15 Messiah Hampton playing again, but not until garbage time.

Based on Hythloday's scouting report of Michigan's games against prior opponents, running on first down to set up second and short was the best offensive strategy.

However, Oregon's advantage in the passing game and weak running game meant they needed to leverage early downs to take deep shots and only run to keep the defense honest.

Prior to garbage time I attribute one failed drive directly to issues with the offensive line and three to play calling decisions. This indicates with different strategy there was a reasonable chance to put the game away halfway through the third quarter.

Though it happened during garbage time, starting RG #55 Douglas Utu was shaken up late in the game and did not return. He was replaced by sophomore OL #50 Demetri Manning. I'll be keeping a sharp eye on the availability reports this week.

Michigan's only hope to win this game was to make far more substantial changes to their personnel use and play calling, see Hythloday's scouting report. Without doing this they had essentially surrendered before kickoff… and then their most productive wide receiver was lost in the first quarter.

Though Michigan could reliably pick up positive gains on the ground, outside of their single super-explosive run they averaged only 4.6 YPC, not enough to sustain drives without a functioning passing game.

The mistakes made by the Ducks' defense were not systemic, there were a smattering of assignment errors at each level, and mobile quarterbacks like the Wolverines' will always cause problems.

In the absence of OLB #44 Tuioti the most common front for Oregon had DE #47 Elijah Rushing playing opposite OLB #10 Mateo Uiagalelei. There was also some use of 3-0-3 "bear" fronts with three defensive tackles. The staff continued to use OLB #31 Nasir Wyatt as a pass rush specialist rather than a regular part of the edge rotation. Against heavier offensive personnel when the defense went to a more classic 3-4 look freshman OLB #41 Dutch Horisk played in Tuioti's strongside "Jack" linebacker spot.

There was an interesting change up in the secondary with DB #5 Davon Benjamin continued to see action as a dime back but was replaced in the rotation at nickel by fellow freshman DB #24 Jett Washington. Up until now Washington had seen occasional duty at boundary safety, but in this game that was handled primarily by DB #12 Peyton Woodward with DB #22 Devin Jackson rotating in as relief. Whether this new "heavy nickel" was a one-off or a more permanent change I don't know yet.

#2742. Sunday Night Football: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase torch Steelers in 38-18 Bengals victory

The Bengals wanted to create a special “white out” environment for Sunday’s game, with the home team wearing its “White Bengal” uniform and helmet.

After the performance against the Steelers, they may want to make that alternate kit permanent.

Quarterback Joe Burrow and receiver Ja’Marr Chase were stellar on Sunday night, with Cincinnati defeating division-rival Pittsburgh 38-18.

In just the first half, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns before finishing the contest 35-of-44 for 409 yards with four TDs. Joe Flacco came in for mop-up duty midway through the final period.

Burrow also tied Peyton Manning’s record streak of five consecutive games of at least four touchdowns.

As he often is, Chase was Burrow’s favorite target, catching 11 passes for 231 yards. While Chase didn’t have a touchdown himself, he caught deep bombs of 53 and 43 yards that helped set up scores.

It was the third-highest output of Chase’s career and the fourth time he’s gone over 200 yards in a regular-season game.

The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions, and would have made it all five if Evan McPherson had hit his 43-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide right. That was McPherson’s first missed kick of the season.

But McPherson had opened the scoring with a 24-yard field goal to cap the opening drive. Drew Sample had a 3-yard TD catch, Chase Brown had a 2-yard score, and Dohnte Meyers had a 15-yard touchdown reception to give the Bengals a 24-3 halftime lead.

Brown caught his second touchdown in the third quarter to make it 31-3. And Samaje Perine closed the Bengals’ scoring with his 1-yard touchdown run with 10:08 left in the fourth quarter.

As well as Cincinnati’s offense played, the defense may have been better. Aaron Rodgers started the contest 0-of-8 passing, with his first completion not coming until there was 4:31 left in the second quarter.

Pittsburgh had just four first downs and 40 total yards at halftime.

Rodgers ended the night 15-of-29 for 143 yards with two touchdowns, both of which came in the fourth quarter after the game was out of reach. Rodgers was also sacked three times.

With the win, the Bengals are now 7-2 on the season and have sole possession of first place in the AFC North. They will have an extra day to prepare, as they’ll face the Commanders next Monday night.

The Steelers fall to 6-3 and will be on the road to face the Eagles next Sunday afternoon.

#2741. Always one of a kind, Oubre reflects on Sixers stint, why he chose Pacers

Always one of a kind, Oubre reflects on Sixers stint, why he chose Pacers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Kelly Oubre Jr. experience switched sides Sunday afternoon at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Back in Philadelphia with the visiting Pacers, Oubre was his usual self. There's never any risk of mistaking Oubre for somebody else.

"Love him," Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle said pregame. "Such an upbeat guy. He's such a unique person. Love the wardrobe, all the different stuff. He's a very authentically one-of-a-kind type guy."

Carlise then detailed Oubre's various basketball qualities, some of which he showed in Indiana's 131-124 loss. The 30-year-old lefty wing scored 16 points and grabbed four rebounds. His day also included a theatrical imitation of Jaylen Brown's off-arm push after the Sixers' star was whistled for an offensive foul.

Sixers fans grew familiiar with Oubre's strengths, weaknesses and eccentricities during his three seasons as a Sixer. He wound up becoming the team's third-longest tenured player behind only Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Oubre played 178 regular-season games and averaged 14.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 steals.

After the Sixers replaced president of basketball operations Daryl Morey with Mike Gansey, Oubre signed a two-year contract with the Pacers in free agency.

"Mike came over from Cleveland and I heard whispers that he wanted some of his Cleveland guys," Oubre said before the game in the visitors' locker room. "And I was like, 'OK, cool. I'm a Philly guy. So I guess when he comes over, I will no longer be a Philly guy.' That was kind of the situation at hand.

"No bad blood because business is business at the end of the day. They have a great team over there, and they put together a team that they think is the best for them. I'll be all right elsewhere. I figured it out."

Oubre thought Indiana made sense as his next stop.

"It was the pace, the culture, the attitude that this team has," he said. "It's a fast-paced style of basketball. It's a bunch of guys who work collectively as a unit and kind of figure it out from there.

"I thought that would be a great opportunity for me to come and and kind of free-flow play, not have to think. I was wrong. Been thinking a lot, but I'm starting to figure it out and starting to get my rhythm here. … It's a great culture. Coach Rick Carlisle is a legend, Hall of Fame coach. And they wanted me. I love people who want me."

As Oubre settled into a new city, the Sixers had a stunning, transformational summer.

Gansey traded for Jaylen Brown, signed LeBron James, and added veteran role players like (former Cavalier) Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Oubre followed along.

"It was must-see TV, like (for) everybody else," he said. "As a basketball fan, it was pretty cool to see where I was kind of reinvent and get new life and new energy. So I was happy with that. Would I have loved to be a part of it? Of course.

"But at the end of the day, I'm a grown man and I've got to keep it moving and figure it out for myself. It was entertaining. … I'm kind of happy for all the people that have sacrificed over these years. … I'm trying to put a road block in that road for y'all."

Oubre joined the Sixers on a minimum-salary deal in September of 2023 after averaging 20.3 points the past season with the Hornets. Head coach Nick Nurse pitched Oubre on his potential to be a valuable, multi-dimensional player for good teams.

"I was literally about to be done with basketball," he said. "Coach Nurse called me multiple times and said, 'I want you to play for me.' And I was like, 'You know what? This guy really seems to care. He really wants me.' So thank you for just pulling me out of that pit and that hole that I was in four years ago. I got some new life in my basketball career.

"I'm always thankful for that and I love Nurse for that. Just appreciative for my time here. The battle wounds and scars that I've been able to build up, it made me a better man."

Throughout his Sixers stint, Oubre often spoke of growth, evolution, adaptation and self-discovery.

He talked again Sunday about his desire to "Be water" and how life as a Sixer changed him.

"I grew a lot, man," Oubre said. "Just the mental fortitude of being able to withstand adversity. Being able to wake up and not necessarily know which soliders are going to battle, just having to put on different hats on any given night. At first it was challenging, because I'm thinking about all the logistics and things and like, 'This is not what they asked me to do.' But at the end of the day, I just bought into being somebody that can be like water and grow with the team.

"It's been a blessing to be able to play with (VJ Edgecombe), be able to watch Tyrese (Maxey) ascend. Those are the guys where we were front line a lot. Just going through war with those guys was amazing. It just taught me mental fortitude. If I can make it through this, I can make it through anything."

Oubre felt he developed a meaningful connection with the Philadelphia fan base over his three years.

"When they talk about the City of Brotherly Love, I think they're talking about your soul, not necessarily about what you can offer them and what you do," he said. "Everybody in this city works hard. They wake up, go to work, keep the city going. And us as the prima donna basketball players, the least we can do is go hard and sacrifice for them so that they have something to cheer about when they come home from work.

"I think that was the relationship that we had. I'm forever indebted and forever grateful to the people in the city of Philadelphia."

#2740. Big Ten Football Power Rankings narrows in on the correct order

Indiana picked up a huge win and crushed USC's hopes and dreams of a CFP berth. Iowa and UCLA continued to chug along, while Wisconsin and Minnesota suffered ugly defeats.

There are now just two weeks left in the regular season. Here are our latest Big Ten Power Rankings.

Oof. That's a bad loss. Just a month after Luke Fickell picked up the biggest win of his tenure vs USC, he arguably suffered his worst defeat. Losing to hapless Maryland at this stage in the season with an interim coach is as bad as it gets. It might even be enough to put him back on the hot seat.

Jedd Fisch's Huskies have reached bowl eligibility, as they have won three of their last four. They now host Indiana in a game in which a majority of the Big Ten will be rooting for the Huskies, as several teams need Indiana to lose in order to have a chance at reaching the Big Ten Championship.

Illinois couldn't get the job done on Friday night in Los Angeles. However, the Fighting Illini defense played an inspired game. Illinois only trailed 12-7 heading into the fourth quarter despite playing in a rain-soaked Rose Bowl. Bret Bielema's squad rounds out the season with senior night against Iowa and a trip to Evanston to face Northwestern.

Despite losing, Northwestern moves up a spot after being competitive with Ohio State despite a rash of injuries. At one point this season, the Wildcats looked like they had a chance to pull off the impossible and make the CFP. While those dreams are certainly dead now, bowl eligibility is still a successful season in Evanston.

Ohio State got back in the win column against Northwestern, but it was far from convincing. The Wildcats were without their starting quarterback and still managed to move the ball. Jeremiah Smith was too much in the end, allowing the Buckeyes to technically stay alive for the CFP, but it would require a miracle.

We've reached the point in the season where it's hard to drop teams in the rankings even despite losses. The Trojans suffered a heartbreaking loss to Indiana in a game they had to have to keep their CFP hopes alive. However, teams 7-10 in our power rankings last week also lost and No. 6 Ohio State now has the same record as USC, but the Trojans won the head-to-head.

If there was any doubt that quarterback Dylan Raiola had turned the corner, Saturday's game proved it. Raiola threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns against a very good Michigan defense. The Ducks will need some help, but their CFP hopes aren't dead yet.

Iowa won a third consecutive game in a convincing rout over Purdue. Iowa only has a trip to Illinois and home game with Nebraska left on the schedule. If Indiana and UCLA both win out, Iowa would finish 10-2 with no Big Ten Championship appearance. Is that good enough for the CFP? Time will tell.

Indiana had the most impressive win of the weekend in the conference, ending Lincoln Riley's CFP hopes. I seriously contemplated bumping the Hoosiers up to No. 1 in the power rankings, but just couldn't pull the trigger on putting a one-loss team above an undefeated one.

UCLA didn't play its cleanest game of the season on Friday night, but still got the job done in the rain against a stubborn Illinois team. The Bruins have likely locked up a CFP spot, as even if they lost out, a two-loss Big Ten team is making the playoff field.

#2738. Jaguars Winners & Losers From Week 10: Parker Washington Explodes In Rivalry Win

It certainly wasn't a blowout, but good teams win and better teams cover. The Jacksonville Jaguars did just that in a 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday.

Despite their record and their roster, the Titans aren't a completely awful team and showed that a bit on Sunday. The Jags had their hands full at times but made the plays when it mattered most to improve to 7-2 for the first time since 1998. Jacksonville is rattling off wins towards a potential play at the AFC's top overall seed and with one of the league's easiest schedules for the rest of the year, things are looking good in Duval County.

There is only one place to start when talking about Jacksonville's third straight win. It's with Parker Washington.

Jacksonville chopped plenty of wood and carried buckets of water on the way to victory. It was the Washington show in Nashville as the former Nittany Lion rattled off a career-high 152 receiving yards. Washington was quiet in the second half but it didn't matter because he did more than enough work in the first half, plucking ball after ball off the heads of hapless Titans defenders.

Washington's big day was part of an even bigger day by quarterback Trevor Lawrence who finished with 352 yards and three touchdowns and eclipsed 20,000 yards passing in Jacksonville. One of those touchdowns came on the first drive of the game where the QB found Washington at the back of the end zone. The only downside of Washington continuing to play so well is that Jacksonville still needs to pay him. As it has after almost every game this season, the price for the third-year receiver has gone up again.

Back in 2023, Washington was selected in the sixth round, making his way up to wide receiver one status in Jacksonville. If Josh Cameron keeps it up, a sixth-rounder himself, he could be well on his way to Washington levels of status.

The rookie Cameron was second on the Jags in receiving with three catches for 67 yards while catching his third touchdown of the year. Cameron also did decently in the return game once more, collecting 142 total return yards with a long of 32. He did get crushed by Tennessee kicker Joey Slye which resulted in a fumble, but those types of plays are few and far between anyway.

There's no question Jacksonville has a loaded wide receiver room. However, Cameron keeps proving he deserves to be on the field. If Brian Thomas Jr. continues to be up and down, Cameron will continue to reap the benefits.

For another Washington comparison: It should really come as no surprise that Bhayshul Tuten had another solid day.

The running back had 113 total yards with 88 yards rushing and his fifth score of the year on the ground. Tuten now has touchdowns on the ground in three straight games and has gone over 100 total yards in two of his last three outings.

Jacksonville made a great call when it turned over the keys to Tuten. His hard-nosed presence unlocks a nastiness in this offense that gives the Jags an edge anytime the ball is in his hands. In the same mold as Washington, Tuten is trusted to make the plays needed to propel the team to victory. He did so on Broadway.

Here is your obligatory Cam Little Rocks section. Little went 4-for-4 on field goals and 4-for-4 on extra points. It's almost indescribable how important it is to have someone as automatic as Little is. The Jags got points on all but two drives (8-10 overall), largely because once the team crosses the 50, they know they can rely on Little to convert.

Much was said about last year's dustup between then 49ers defensive coordinator Rob Salah and Liam Coen. How sweet must it be for Coen to beat Salah last year, only to turn around and drop 40 in Salah's home stadium, now the head coach with the Titans? Running Tuten into the end zone with under two minutes to play had to feel damn good.

Coen has done a tremendous job with the Jags since taking over. It doesn't take this column to tell you that. Jacksonville has cut down on penalties (just two Sunday) and overall boneheaded mistakes. That game was one Lawrence batted-ball interception away from being about as good as you could get, at least offensively. Coen has won 20 of his first 26 games, and is just the third coach to do so in the last 15 years. He is tops in terms of winning percentage over those games in the history of the sport.

Jacksonville is rolling and the head coach is a huge reason why. Keeping his coordinators in place after last year's hiring cycle cannot go unnoticed too. This is the year to make a run. There's no reason to believe right now that Coen isn't the guy to lead it.

Yeah, so that trade for Jessie Bates was a huge one because the safety play in Nashville was subpar. More will be said on the defense below, but Bates proved his worth before ever even taking a snap defensively for Jacksonville. This team needs help on the back end. Luckily, help is ready to play and maybe even sleeping in the facility.

Does anyone want to talk about that Tony Pollard touchdown? No?

Yes, the Titans aren't a great offense. Yes, the Jags have a smothering defense typically. But also yes that the Titans are playing well offensively as of late. The Jags got exposed at times by that offense and especially on Pollard's 32-yard receiving touchdown where he broke through just about the entire Jacksonville defense. Cam Ward and company didn't light Jacksonville up, but that game wasn't the pure defensive domination many might have thought was coming.

There were some solid individual performances though on defense. Travis Hunter had an incredible leaping interception. Ventrell Miller was crushing guys like usual. Dennis Gardeck even looked pretty solid. But this defense needs the help it acquired at the deadline. Overall, no worries probably. But that was not this unit's best performance of the year at all.

There were no DaVon Hamilton-level injuries following Sunday's game, but that doesn't mean the Jags got out of Nashville unscathed. The big injury question mark after that game was with a knee injury to Robert Hainsey. You can make the case that Hainsey maybe shouldn't even be out there, but it's a blow to the team's overall depth if he is down for a while. This specific injury sort of amplifies a questionable lack of offensive line talent acquired at the trade deadline from the front office. Can't complain about that defensive haul, but still.

In a much less catastrophic way, defensive end Danny Striggow left with a concussion. He looked to be getting some solid reps out there before he was ruled out. Again, depth is always helpful especially if the team is going to keep adding games in the playoffs.

Nothing world-ending, but something to monitor as we keep this thing chugging along.

#2737. Jahmyr Gibbs in Hall of Fame company with a long list of statistical achievements

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had another phenomenal game on Sunday, and in his fourth NFL season he has hit a long list of statistical milestones that only Hall of Famers have reached before him.

In Sunday’s 35-10 win over the Patriots, Gibbs carried 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns, and added seven catches for 99 yards. After the game, the NFL distributed a list of Gibbs’ stats that show him either equaling or exceeding the accomplishments of some of the greatest running backs ever to play the game. Among Gibbs’ milestones:

Gibbs has the most touchdowns in NFL history in a player’s first four seasons. He has now scored 62 touchdowns (50 rushing and 12 receiving), breaking the previous record of Hall of Famer Terrell Davis, who had 61 touchdowns in his first four seasons.

Gibbs’ 50 career rushing touchdowns make him the third player in NFL history to run for 50 touchdowns before turning 25. The other two are Hall of Famers Barry Sanders with 52, and Emmitt Smith with 50. Gibbs doesn’t turn 25 until after this season, so he’s a near-lock to move ahead of Sanders and into first place on the all-time list.

Gibbs and Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson are the only players in NFL history to have multiple games with at least 250 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns before turning 25.

Gibbs, Tomlinson and Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson are the only players to have four games of at least 200 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in their first four seasons.

Gibbs has topped 1,200 scrimmage yards and 10 rushing touchdowns in each of his first four seasons. The only players who have done that before are Tomlinson, Dickerson, Hall of Famer Earl Campbell and future Hall of Famer Adrian Peterson.

Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown have played 24 games together in which they’ve both scored touchdowns, surpassing Bills Hall of Famers Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed, who both scored in 23 games, for the fourth-most games in which running back-wide receiver teammates both score. All the players ahead of Gibbs and St. Brown are Hall of Famers: Emmitt Smith and Michael Irvin did it 32 times for the Cowboys, Lenny Moore and Raymond Berry did it 31 times for the Colts, and Edgerrin James and Marvin Harrison did it 25 times for the Colts.

Only three and a half seasons into his NFL career, it’s too early to put Gibbs in the Hall of Fame. But everything about the way he has played so far indicates that some day he’ll have a bust in Canton.

#2735. Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win

Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night.

They overcame a first-quarter deficit as high as 17 points and earned a 123-112 home win over the Raptors. The Sixers moved to 10-3 and Toronto fell to 5-7.

Tyrese Maxey had 27 points and eight assists. Joel Embiid added 20 points.

Jaylen Brown tallied 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe posted 15 points, eight rebounds and a season-high eight assists. Anfernee Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range.

RJ Barrett recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds. Immanuel Quickley had 26 points and six assists.

The Sixers were without LeBron James (low back/sciatica management), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear).

The team told reporters Thursday morning that Bona will be re-evaluated in approximately one week and that Barlow participated in shootaround. The 23-year-old forward also went through a pregame workout on the Xfinity Mobile Arena floor. There's no formal timetable for his return.

Toronto's sidelined players included Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes.

The Sixers will face the Pacers on Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Here are observations on their victory over the Raptors:

Dean Wade began the game in James' normal spot. The Sixers started slowly, missing their first foul field goals and opening 1 for 8 from three-point range.

He stayed down after setting a ball screen and having an apparent knee-to-knee collision with Ja'Kobe Walter. The Sixers called timeout with 8:30 left in the first quarter and Embiid grabbed at his right knee. He eventually rose with assistance from teammates and Sixers head athletic trainer Kevin Johnson, then limped back to the locker room. Jabari Walker entered.

At the 5:26 mark of the first quarter, Embiid checked back in to cheers from the home fans.

"I knew that he didn't twist it or anything," Maxey said. "I knew it was a knee-to-knee, so I wasn't too worried. He kept saying, 'I just got kneed.' That still hurts, though."

Embiid ended up logging 28 minutes, though he certainly wanted to play more.

"He was very, very motivated to play," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "It was hard to get him out for his scheduled rests tonight, which is a good problem sometimes."

While Embiid's return was a major positive development, the Sixers fell further behind. The Raptors' lead swelled to 32-16 with a Jamison Battle three-pointer and Nurse burned a timeout.

Simons sunk a buzzer-beating three to conclude the first quarter, cutting the Sixers' deficit to nine points.

"Those are big momentum plays that usually have some weight to them and carry you into the next moment," Nurse said.

The Sixers kept rolling against a shorthanded Toronto team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Simons nailed a triple to kick off the scoring in the second quarter. Brown buried a mid-range jumper and Edgecombe jammed in a crowd-pleasing dunk to give the Sixers a 35-34 edge.

Brown and Edgecombe shined in the second quarter both as individuals and as a duo. The Sixers need Edgecombe to attack a bit more offensively when he shares the floor with Brown and bench players. It doesn't hurt for the second-year guard to have that clarity about his role in those units.

"He's one of our better playmakers," Maxey said of Edgecombe. "He's really good at getting downhill and creating for himself and others."

The Sixers' only three bench rotation players were Walker, Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (11 points, five assists). In addition to Walker, Wade got center minutes behind Embiid.

Embiid picked up his third foul with 2:23 left in the second quarter and had to take a seat. The teams were tied at 60 apiece through two periods.

The game remained even for much of the third, but Maxey fueled an 11-0 Sixers run late in the quarter.

His speed and the Sixers' collective focus on pushing the pace whenever possible allowed the team to get regular points before Toronto could set its defense. Maxey zoomed in for a layup, then tossed the ball ahead to Brown for an easy bucket. Brown assisted a Simons three. Walker converted a fast-break lay-in and canned a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter. All of a sudden, the Sixers held a 101-87 lead.

Brown, Edgecombe and the bench gave the Sixers more good minutes early in the fourth quarter. They sealed the deal without any late drama. And the fans chanting for a Tacko Fall appearance got their wish with a final-minute entrance by the 7-foot-6 center.

#2733. Fernando Mendoza: It's good to learn from getting punched in the face

Fernando Mendoza didn’t look overmatched early in his first NFL start, but the road got tougher for the Raiders’ rookie quarterback over the final three quarters of Sunday’s game against the Seahawks.

Mendoza capped the team’s first offensive possession with a touchdown run and led the Raiders to a field goal on their second possession, but the Raiders would pick up just 68 yards and three points over the rest of their 21-13 home loss. Things got particularly bad in the second half as the Raiders failed to pick up a first down while losing 17 yards over their first five post-halftime possessions.

Mendoza was sacked six times and hit 12 times over the course of the game, but found a way to put a positive spin on the experience when he spoke to reporters after the game.

“The Seahawks have a fantastic defense, we’ve seen it all season,” Mendoza said, via the team’s website. “A lot of credit to them. . . . It’s good to get punched in the face because now it’s a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and [become] a future hopeful leader of this offense.”

The Broncos are next up for the Raiders, which means Mendoza will face another experienced and accomplished defense that could teach him some painful lessons that he uses to steel himself for future success as an NFL quarterback.

#2732. Mike Macdonald praises Tory Horton's "tremendous play" on late kickoff return

After the Raiders cut the Seahawks’ lead to 21-13 by kicking a field goal with 2:04 left in Sunday’s game, they wanted to force a touchback that would allow them to use the two-minute warning as a third timeout in hopes of getting the ball back.

Seahawks wide receiver Tory Horton made sure that didn’t happen. Horton perfectly timed a leap that allowed him to bat a kickoff that was sailing long into the end zone. Horton stepped out of bounds upon coming down, so he motioned for Rashid Shaheed to return it into the field of play and Shaheed was tackled with 1:59 left to accomplish the Seahawks’ goal of burning the Raiders’ extra chance to stop the clock.

Horton was flagged for an illegal bat of the ball, but the Raiders declined the penalty as it would have forced a re-kick that took more time off the clock and head coach Mike Macdonald praised Horton’s quick thinking in his postgame press conference.

“It was a tremendous play,” Macdonald said, via the team’s website. “Tory’s actually trying to catch that ball, albeit with one hand. Just an incredible play. With George Holani going down, we had to take [Jadarian Price] off of kickoff returns, so those are guys that haven’t necessarily practiced a bunch in a while, especially with this game plan. So to be able to step in and be able to execute some of those critical situations is some great stuff by them, great job by our coaches, and it really helped us close the game out. . . . We told them that was the situation going. Now, there’s a difference between catching it 8 yards deep in the end zone and making a play like that, which is just some really, really great stuff.”

The Seahawks were likely to win the game regardless of how the kickoff played out, but Horton made closing things out easier and his effort will be on the minds of many people around the league if they find themselves in a similar situation.

#2731. Will Rams offensive lineman recover for Week 12?

The Los Angeles Rams beat the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, but they lost their starting center Coleman Shelton and back-up center Dylan McMahon. It was an unbelievable occurrence, as the injuries mount up for L.A., but they were able to win and now get the bye week to rest.

For the Rams, they have to hope they are healthier for their Week 12 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. If the Rams centers are ready by then, they may have to sign some new faces.

The injuries keep piling up for the Rams, but they are on a four game win streak and will spend the next week hoping to get some guys back as they prepare for an end of season run. These next few weeks will likely determine if the Rams make the playoffs or not. Having their centers back could make push easier, but they'll play with the guys they have.

"Starting center Coleman Shelton exited early in the first half with a hamstring injury. His replacement, Dylan McMahon, suffered a knee injury shortly before halftime, forcing the Rams into another round of musical chairs.

#2730. Syracuse football: Calvin Russell shows ability and leadership

Earlier this Fall, Syracuse HC Fran Brown was asked about the leaders in his locker room. To the surprise of many, he mentioned freshman wide receiver Calvin Russell.

We knew Calvin Russell could play football. The five-star from Miami had his choice of schools during his recruitment so if Brown had said that Russell was the best player on the team it wouldn't have elicited such a surprise.

On Saturday, Russell tied a Syracuse school-record with 17 receptions for 137 yards and a touchdown. He was credited with two carries for 24 yards and attempted one pass. It's the most receptions for a FBS player since 2024 and the Orange saw the advantage he had in the short passing game and kept feeding him.

An incredibly impressive performance for sure. Even more impressive when we recall that Russell tore his achilles in the spring and some felt Brown needed to just sit him all year to let him heal. You can see why it was important for the Orange to keep Russell engaged during his rehab and what he's showing on the field that shows you why he was a top recruiting target.

It's what we saw after the game that reinforces Brown's claim from earlier this Fall. You don't see Russell talking about the record, but about the team and what winning does for others.

We'll forgive him for not shouting out Tunmise Adeleye by name after the afternoon he had, but when you ask why it's big for Syracuse to get talents like Russell, it's not just what he brings on Saturday. If you're best players can be your leaders, then you can create a culture that carries through your locker room.

This season hasn't been pretty, but when you see a team fight like they've done the last seven games, you can set a foundation to build upon. Of course it sure doesn't hurt to have a future NFL talent to trust with the ball either.

#2726. ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles

'Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker shared the floor for 128 games in Portland. The Trail Blazers won 43 of them.

They sat beside one another in the Sixers' interview room Thursday night after a victory and discussed what the other 85 taught them.

"Whether you've got a big role or a small role, it's hard to win in the NBA," Simons said. "We've seen it firsthand."

Their roles were considerably different then.

Simons was an established starter entrusted with creating and scoring. Walker, a 2022 second-round pick, was trying to establish himself in a rotation. During their three overlapping seasons, Portland went 33-49, 21-61 and 36-46. The Blazers missed the playoffs each year.

Both are now reserves on a Sixers team constructed to contend. In nine games they've both appeared in this season, Philadelphia is 7-2.

They provided 26 points, 11 rebounds and six three-pointers in the Sixers' 123-112 win over the Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. Walker recorded nine points and eight rebounds, including four on the offensive glass.

The Sixers outscored Toronto by 24 points during Simons' 23 minutes. Neither former Blazer committed a turnover.

Their production helped Philadelphia overcome a 17-point first-quarter deficit and improve to 10-3 without LeBron James.

"You learn once you come off the bench to kind of read the game before you get in there," Simons said. "Obviously, we started off kind of slow. You just want to go in, bring some energy, get some stops, get out and run. I think everybody who got off the bench brought energy."

Simons supplied an immediate lift with a deep three-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer. His shot ended an 8-0 Sixers run and trimmed Toronto's lead to nine.

He remained involved during an 11-0 burst late in the third quarter, knocking down a three and setting up Walker for a basket. Walker then made a three early in the fourth before Simons scored on the Sixers' next possession.

When Toronto pulled within six with less than five minutes remaining, Simons answered with his fifth three-pointer.

Making those shots is the most obvious way Simons can help a roster already featuring James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. He said the Sixers have not made him feel as though every opportunity must go in.

"They encourage us to keep shooting the ball," Simons said. "Knowing that a team has that much confidence in us to keep shooting makes the game that much easier. Whether you miss or make, as long as we get the right shots in the right moments, I think everybody can live with the misses and makes."

Simons spent seven seasons in Portland before playing last year with Boston and Chicago. His move to Philadelphia reunited him with Walker and Rayan Rupert, another former Blazer who joined the Sixers on a two-way contract during the offseason.

Knowing familiar faces awaited him helped Simons enter another new locker room.

"It made the transition seamless," he said. "Just being able to have some comfortability with guys that I played with for multiple years. It's been fun, kind of feeling like a little bit of old times. Me, Bari and Rups have been through a lot."

Walker's path to Philadelphia began a year earlier and required an additional step.

After playing 188 games over three seasons with Portland, Walker signed a two-way contract with the Sixers in July 2025. He earned a standard contract in February and has since pushed his way into the backup-center conversation despite standing 6-foot-7.

Walker believes some of the work he did on losing teams was easily missed.

"When I first got to the league, I was part of a rebuilding process," he said. "I just felt like some of the little things I did didn't always get noticed when you're losing. I told myself, if I ever got to be part of a winning organization, then I'd go out and expand my abilities."

Rebounding has made Walker difficult for Nick Nurse to overlook.

Walker credited his timing and strong hands to lessons passed down by his father, former NBA center Samaki Walker. Those instincts have become especially useful while the Sixers piece together their frontcourt behind Embiid.

"Rebounding is a skill I kind of honed in on," Walker said. "My dad was a good rebounder. He was known for his rebounding and his timing. I think it's just a gift that he transferred to me."

Walker has made it clear that he expected to earn a role this season.

"I don't know if I was delusional, but I always felt like I was going to play and I was going to be a part," he said. "I read something where they said it's a surprise, but if you were around me this summer, it wouldn't be a surprise. This is expected, and I just want to continue to get better."

The freedom Simons once had in Portland is no longer necessary. Walker does not need a high volume of touches, either. Both understand that playing beside the Sixers' stars requires shooting when open, moving the ball and handling the less glamorous work.

"You've got to find ways to impact the game multiple ways, even if you're not scoring," Simons said. "Whether it's cutting, making the right read and pass to Joel, being the right swing pass to VJ, boxing out on defense or just being in the right position."

Their opportunities will fluctuate. Simons may take nine shots one night and only a few the next. Walker's minutes will depend on matchups and the health of Philadelphia's frontcourt.

Winning has changed what they are being asked to do. Their three years together in Portland taught them why the adjustment is worthwhile.

"You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you're winning," Simons said. "That's something you can't take for granted."

#2725. After the loss to the Bills, it feels like Aaron Glenn’s fate is sealed

"I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs."

That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the television series, The Office.

Michael Scott didn't end up losing his job as branch manager of Dunder-Mifflin in the end. Nevertheless, the review remains relatable.

Sometimes people can improve their job performance, but other times you reach a realization that they just aren't capable of doing it.

We are past that stage with Aaron Glenn. We can point to any number of dubious marks of his resume as Jets head coach. He is now 5-22, sporting a worse winning percentage as an NFL head coach than Hue Jackson. Glenn now has more than twice as many double digit point losses than he has wins. The latest defeat was the ugly 31-12 blowout at the hands of the Buffalo Bills in Week 10.

There isn't much drama left surrounding Glenn. Barring an unexpected late season surge, he will not retain his job as Jets head coach for a third year. Even if there is a late season winning streak, it still might not be enough.

NFL teams don't reassign their coach to a different department. Coaching contracts aren't written that way, and practical considerations make the sort of demotion recommended for Scott unviable.

Glenn will be let go. He will make enough money to leave football if he so chooses. If he decides to continue his coaching career, he will be an in demand candidates for teams seeking a new defensive coordinator.

In the meantime, we will have to endure seven more games. That will be no easy task.

I am sure the Jets will invent new ways to lose along the way.

In some ways, the Jets' Week 10 loss to the Bills was familiar. Like a week earlier against the Chiefs, the Jets stayed competitive through one half of football. Their offense settled for field goals instead of scoring touchdowns. Then things fell apart in the second half.

This loss still was in many ways different from what we have seen before. Leave it to the Aaron Glenn Jets to lose by three scores in a game where they had an equal number of first downs to their opponent and only 13 fewer total yards.

The Jets showed many of the coaching flaws that have plagued the team throughout the season.

On offense this team shows no understanding of how to use its talent to the greatest effect. At this point, it feels like salary is the main consideration driving the decision to lean on Breece Hall as the lead back over Braelon Allen. It certainly isn't performance. The Jets can lean on saying, "A starter can't lose his job to injury," all they want. Whether or not Hall missed time from injury, Allen has outplayed him.

The Jets struggle just as much to play to their strengths in the passing game. It's easy to dismiss Kenyon Sadiq's lack of a role as a developing rookie showing inconsistency. But when backup wide receiver Isaiah Williams gets 7 targets, and a mismatch like Sadiq only gets 2, it speaks to mistaken priorities in the game plan.

The Jets can't put the ball in the end zone. There are no simple explanations for that. I'm sure it didn't help that they had a fourth round rookie quarterback with zero first team reps through the week playing half the game, but the inability to score touchdowns has been a season-long problem. Anyone watching the team would likely conclude that play calling has been a factor.

On the defensive side of the ball, the Jets are simply playing bad football. Aaron Glenn referred to play calling as his superpower, but Glenn's inability to orchestrate this defense has him looking like a mere mortal.

I think there's a danger for the Jets in blaming all of their problems on coaching. The roster isn't good enough just yet. Part of this is that the team had a long way to rebuild after their attempts to win a Super Bowl around Aaron Rodgers failed. Part of it is the team has made too many personnel misfires. The Jets need to ask themselves hard questions about the way they do business on many levels as they chart out their future.

For now, though, the coaching is the obvious and glaring problem at the center of everyone's attention.

Seven games remain, and unlike binging a television show, we can't just skip ahead to the next season when we don't like what we are seeing.

#2724. Travis Hunter now has two games with a catch and an interception. Deion Sanders had nine.

Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter intercepted a pass on Sunday against the Titans, and doing his part-time job as a wide receiver, he also caught two passes. It was the second time Hunter has both caught and intercepted a pass in the same game.

That’s a rare feat in the modern NFL, where few players play both ways. It’s been four years since any player other than Hunter had both a catch and an interception in the same game. The last player to do it was New England’s Marcus Jones, who did it twice in 2022.

Since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, the player who has had both a catch and an interception in the same game the most times is Hunter’s college coach, Deion Sanders, who did it nine times. Sanders did it three times while playing for the Falcons and six times while playing for the Cowboys.

Hunter is primarily a defensive player: He played 56 defensive snaps and only six offensive snaps on Sunday, and that’s been typical for him this season. Overall in 2026, Hunter has played 84 percent of the Jaguars’ defensive snaps and 9 percent of the Jaguars’ offensive snaps. But the Jaguars say they view Hunter as a two-way player for the long term, so there’s a good chance that he’ll have more games with both a catch and an interception, and perhaps eclipse Sanders’ modern-era record of nine such games.

But Hunter is unlikely to break the all-time record of Packers Hall of Famer Don Hutson, who had 21 games with both a catch and an interception between 1940 and 1945. Hutson had some statistics that don’t look possible, such as the game when he outscored the Chicago Cardinals all by himself with six catches for 86 yards and two touchdowns, plus two interceptions for 84 return yards and a pick-six, in a 35-14 Packers victory. Hutson was by far the best receiver of his era and one of the best defensive players of his era, and he was also a pretty good kicker by the standards of the 1940s. There will never be another Don Hutson.

What Hunter is doing in 2026, however, is a special accomplishment that also deserves celebration. There’s no one else playing the game in quite the same way Hunter is playing it.

#2722. Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status

Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury.

Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation.

The Patriots started Sunday's game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart.

Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye's right ankle.

He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team's medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game.

Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out.

Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye's status during their post-game media availability.

"Obviously, he wasn't able to finish the game, so we'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has," Vrabel said at the podium.

"I know that it was a low leg injury. I don't know the exact details of it but I know he couldn't go back in. … He couldn't function. Couldn't play. Couldn't run. Couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level."

Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room.

"I talked to him," Campbell told MassLive's Mark Daniels. "He's in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he's going to be fine. He's a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he's going to attack it full head of steam and come back better."

The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team's arrival on Monday.

[UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a "significant lower leg injury" that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario.

[UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions.

[UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel.

"He'll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."

[UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would "almost certainly" be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport.

"Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions," safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game.

The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future.

What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period.

DeVito described his and the offense's performance after he took over for Maye as "not good enough." The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots' upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye.

[UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.

#2721. Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid

Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Jaylen Brown-Tyrese Maxey duo starred, LeBron James reached another milestone, and the Sixers earned a win without Joel Embiid on Sunday afternoon.

They improved to 11-3 on the season with a 131-124 victory over the Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Brown scored 31 points and Maxey posted 27.

LeBron James had 15 points and 11 assists. He passed Jason Kidd on Sunday for third in NBA history with 12,092 assists.

Pascal Siakam scored 31 points for the 5-9 Pacers.

On the first day of a back-to-back, the Sixers were down Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pacers' injured players included Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard.

The Sixers will face the Nets on Monday night in Brooklyn. Here are observations on their win over the Pacers:

Jabari Walker started for the first time this season, opening the game at center. He's been in the Sixers' rotation the past five games since Bona's injury.

Walker set up the Sixers' first basket, swiping a steal and then tossing the ball ahead to Maxey for a fast-break dunk. Maxey and Brown both began well and combined to score all of the Sixers' first 15 points.

Though he conceded five inches to 7-foot Pacers center Ivica Zubac, Walker was solid in his first stint. He got an early post stop on Zubac and then snatched a strong defensive rebound.

Dean Wade was next up for the Sixers at the five. He sunk a three-pointer on his first shot to give the team a 20-16 lead.

Walker ended up playing 25 minutes and posting 11 points and seven rebounds. Going back to the preseason, his stock has steadily risen.

"Here we are again after another game saying Jabari played very well," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "He plays hard, he rebounds, he's got another level of confidence with his shooting this year.

"It's kind of wash, rinse and repeat again with him (today). He was great. … Jabari went in there and battled (Zubac). I thought he certainly matched him, if not outplayed him, which is a heck of a job."

Wade had 12 points and seven boards in 35 minutes. Overall, the Sixers' lack of healthy conventional centers is still a clear deficiency. Of course, everything should be simpler once Embiid is back in action.

The Sixers' defense did not have a sparkling start. The Pacers tallied 35 points in the first quarter and shot 62.5 percent from the field.

Brown helped the Sixers avoid a substantial deficit by draining all sorts of jumpers. He rarely appears bothered by close contests. Brown moved to 7 for 9 from the floor when he knocked down a three early in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's triple knotted the contest up at 37-all.

Nurse needed to stray from his Plan A rotation when VJ Edgecombe picked up his third foul with 9:56 left in the second quarter. Labaron Philon Jr., who got a game with the G League's Delaware Blue Coats on Friday night, subbed in.

For a rookie guard, Philon has looked comfortable and confident on offense in most of his NBA appearances. He swished a long-range jumper in the second quarter and saw a floater rim out.

Brown reached the 20-point mark and put the Sixers up one with a slam assisted by James late in the second quarter.

He ran into serious foul trouble in the third quarter. Brown was whistled for his fourth foul with 9:53 left in the period for an off-arm shove on Aaron Nesmith. Wade entered and Brown exited.

The Sixers' slim lead didn't slip away. Walker nailed threes on consecutive possessions and Maxey jammed in a dunk.

Soon after, Tacko Fall came in for his first meaningful minutes as a Sixer. The 7-foot-6 two-way contract player grabbed an offensive board off a missed Edgecombe free throw, which drew one of the day's loudest cheers. With Fall on the floor, Maxey and James connected on an alley-oop that extended the Sixers' lead to 82-73.

When the Sixers tried to sit in a zone, Fall was called for a defensive three-second violation. Whatever the scheme, most of Fall's defensive work will come around the paint. He certainly has exceptional physical traits as a rim protector and is not nimble on the perimeter.

Fall logged five scoreless third-quarter minutes and recorded three rebounds. The Sixers outscored Indiana by a point with Fall on the court. Given Fall is occupying a (two-way) roster slot and the Sixers are so depleted at center, it made sense to see a bit of what he can do outside of garbage time. While five minutes isn't enough for any grand conclusions, it's very safe to say Fall is a unique player.

"I'm 7-6, so I can change the game in so many ways," Fall said. "Offensively, setting screens, making sure guys get open, being an easy target for lobs. Defensively, I feel like I've always been an elite rim protector and I've worked on my body a lot to be able to move a lot better."

Nurse praised Fall's outing, saying he "gave us some great minutes and a nice lift."

Fall is appreciative of his first NBA opportunity since the 2021-22 season.

"I've worked very hard," he said. "God has brought me back here and I'm thankful. And I'm ready. Whenever my name is called, I'm going to go out there and do my job."

The Sixers built their advantage to 102-87 with a Brown three early in the fourth quarter. They couldn't cruise to a blowout, though.

Siakam kept hurting the Sixers as a driver and had a highly efficient fourth quarter, scoring 19 points on 7-for-9 shooting. Quenton Jackson's layup trimmed Indiana's deficit to 119-115.

The Sixers ultimately held off the Pacers' push.

Caldwell-Pope canned a three, Wade threw down an and-one dunk, and James checked off his milestone assist with a late dish to Edgecombe for a layup.
